Here are the key contributions of **"Attention Is All You Need"** (Vaswani et al., 2017), drawn from our wiki:

---

## 1. The Transformer Architecture
The paper introduced the **first sequence transduction model built entirely on attention**, removing recurrence (RNNs/LSTMs) and convolutions entirely. This was the central conceptual break from prior SOTA models like RNN/LSTM/GRU and ConvS2S.
→ [[transformer-architecture]]

---

## 2. Scaled Dot-Product Attention
A fast, efficient attention formula:
```
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKᵀ / √d_k) · V
```
The `√d_k` scaling prevents softmax saturation at large dimensions. Compared to additive (Bahdanau) attention, it is significantly faster and more memory-efficient due to optimized matrix multiplication.
→ [[scaled-dot-product-attention]]

---

## 3. Multi-Head Attention
Instead of a single attention function, the paper runs **h parallel attention heads** on different linear projections of Q/K/V, then concatenates results. This lets the model jointly attend to information from **different representation subspaces**, which a single averaged attention head cannot do. The paper found 8 heads optimal (25.8 BLEU), with diminishing returns beyond that.
→ [[multi-head-attention]]

---

## 4. Full Parallelization
By replacing recurrent layers with self-attention, the Transformer enables **fully parallel training** — no sequential hidden state dependencies. This collapses the maximum dependency path between any two positions from O(n) to **O(1)**, making long-range dependencies dramatically easier to learn.

| Layer Type | Sequential Ops | Max Path Length |
|---|---|---|
| Self-Attention | O(1) | O(1) |
| Recurrent (RNN) | O(n) | O(n) |

---

## 5. Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
Since self-attention is permutation-invariant (treats input as a set), the paper added **fixed sinusoidal position signals** to embeddings. The key property: PE(pos+k) is a linear function of PE(pos), giving the model relative position awareness. Interestingly, learned embeddings performed nearly identically (BLEU 25.8 vs 25.7).
→ [[positional-encoding]]

---

## 6. SOTA Results at Lower Cost
- **WMT 2014 EN→DE:** 28.4 BLEU — **+2 BLEU** over prior ensemble SOTA
- **WMT 2014 EN→FR:** 41.8 BLEU — new single-model SOTA, trained in **3.5 days on 8 P100s**
- **WSJ Parsing:** 92.7 F1 — competitive without task-specific tuning

The big model beat prior SOTA at a fraction of the training cost, validating the efficiency claims.

---

**Bottom line:** The paper's lasting contribution is proving that attention alone is sufficient — and superior — for sequence modeling, which directly enabled BERT, GPT, and every major LLM that followed.
